Overview

This repository serves as a centralised archive for the data analysis dashboards I have created. It is intended to store, organise, and showcase dashboards developed across different projects, tools, and datasets.

The dashboards focus on transforming raw data into meaningful insights through visualisations, summary metrics, and analytical reporting.

Purpose

The primary purpose of this repository is to:

- Preserve completed dashboards for future reference
- Track progress and growth in data analysis and visualisation skills
- Showcase practical dashboard projects for learning and portfolio use

Contents

Each folder or file in this repository represents a standalone dashboard project and may include:

- Dashboard files (e.g., Power BI, Excel, Tableau, or Python-based dashboards)
- Supporting datasets (where applicable)
- Brief notes explaining the objective and insights of each dashboard

Tools and Technologies

Dashboards in this repository may be created using one or more of the following tools:

- Excel
- Power BI
- Python (Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Streamlit)
- SQL
- Other data visualisation or analytics tools as applicable

Usage

This repository is primarily for documentation and portfolio purposes. Files can be explored to understand how different datasets were analyzed and visualized.

Notes

Datasets used may be publicly available, simulated, or anonymised for learning and demonstration purposes.

---

This repository will be updated regularly as new dashboards are created.

draft.body:
Effective business decisions stem from a clear process that transforms raw data into actionable insights. The "Data-Analysis-Dashboard" repository showcases my structured workflow designed to deliver decision-ready analytics.

You can explore the project here: https://github.com/alumond/Data-Analysis-Dashboard

Each project follows a systematic workflow. It begins with data cleaning, transforming raw information into a reliable foundation. Next, analytical processing uncovers patterns and relationships. Finally, visualization presents these findings as dynamic charts and metrics within a user-friendly dashboard.

Consider tracking sales or marketing performance. Instead of manual spreadsheet analysis, a dashboard built with this workflow instantly displays critical trends and metrics. This allows business leaders to quickly identify areas for improvement or confirm successful strategies, supporting proactive growth.

Unlike reports that only present data, these dashboards transform complex raw information into digestible insights. They simplify trend exploration and directly support decision-making. This structured workflow ensures data becomes a valuable asset for business growth, rather than just an archive.

The repository demonstrates this systematic approach, turning raw data into clear, actionable insights essential for informed business decisions.

draft.visual_prompt:
A clear, concise process map illustrating the dashboard workflow: 1. Input: Raw Data (represented by unorganized data icon). 2. Step: Data Cleaning (represented by a cleaning icon or filter icon). 3. Step: Analytical Processing (represented by a gears icon or analysis icon). 4. Step: Visualization (represented by a dashboard icon with charts). 5. Output: Actionable Insights & Decision Support (represented by a lightbulb icon or target icon). Arrows connect each step sequentially. Use simple, readable labels for each stage.
Required visual direction: Preserve the highest native image quality. Capture app screens at 3x pixel density, normally 4800x3360 lossless PNG. Use imagegen at its highest available native quality. Never upscale small images or use lossy recompression. Check sharp edges and text at full size and readable key labels at phone size. Polished editorial graphics and clear data visuals with a strong complete title, generous spacing, short readable captions, and a concrete connection to the post. Codex-generated images must use relevant symbols, icons and diagrams to explain the idea. Give these visuals enough space to be understood at phone size. Keep text to a short title, labels and brief captions. Reject paragraphs in boxes and layouts where icons are only small decorations around text. For workflow posts, visualize the actual workflow discussed in the post: inputs, ordered steps, decisions, handoffs, relevant revision or failure paths, and outputs. Use a process map for sequential steps, a decision flow for branching logic, or swimlanes when ownership across people and tools matters. Show only steps and connections supported by the post and its evidence; label proposed workflows as proposed. Use real portfolio screenshots where relevant and label illustrative data explicitly. Every image must be visually inspected at phone size. Avoid: sketches and hand-drawn illustrations, model drawings and wireframes, generic AI artwork and decorative stick figures, internal drafting notes or placeholder text in artwork, truncated headlines and unlabeled decorative charts, dark 3D boardroom scenes by default, unlabeled abstract metaphors, unreadable tiny UI text, misspelled generated text, neon-by-default, glowing brains and circuit-board cliches, robot faces and generic AI imagery, sparse skeleton diagrams, text-only quote cards, paragraphs in boxes with only decorative icons, synthetic photorealism.
